change.title: claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929 retires on the Claude API Nov 30, 2026; use claude-sonnet-5-5

tasks.reasoning:
The repo calls messages.create through @anthropic-ai/sdk 0.125.0, but the usage map does not record which model it passes. Sonnet 4.5 is a common choice for extraction scripts like this harvest step, so I am attempting the task rather than skipping it. The migration agent should open harvest/lib/extract.ts, plus any config or env file that supplies the model, and check for claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929 or the claude-sonnet-4-5 alias. If found, replace it with claude-sonnet-5-5. While doing so, remove forced tool_choice (any/tool) and thinking {type:'disabled'}, both of which return 400 on Sonnet 5.5. If the model is something else, close the task as a no-op. If it is affected, the extraction harvest fails outright after the retirement date.
This task also resolves these changes. Handle each in the same change, and say in the PR how:
- anthropic:2026-09-28-sonnet-5-5-breaking (other): Code written for Sonnet 5 can break on claude-sonnet-5-5 (thinking disabled, forced tool_choice return 400). claude-sonnet-5-5 is the named replacement. If this migration moves the call to sonnet-5-5, the same edit must drop any thinking-disabled config and forced tool_choice (any/tool), which return 400 on Sonnet 5.5.
  Source: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/release-notes/api
  "Forced tool use (tool_choice types any and tool) returns a 400 error."

callSites.why: messages.create is the only Claude call in the repo. The model id was not captured by the scan. If it is claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929, requests start failing once the model retires on 2026-11-30.

## claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929 retires on the Claude API Nov 30, 2026; use claude-sonnet-5-5 [Not affected]

### Change

No change made. harvest/lib/extract.ts pins EXTRACT_MODEL = 'claude-sonnet-5', not claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929 or the claude-sonnet-4-5 alias. A repo-wide search found no other reference to the retiring model.

No files changed.

### Why

The retirement covers only claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929, and this repo never calls it. The Sonnet 5.5 breaking-change item applies only if a call moves to claude-sonnet-5-5, and this migration doesn't move it.

### Unproven

- I did not run the checks, since nothing changed.

### Behaviour changes

- None. If someone later moves EXTRACT_MODEL to claude-sonnet-5-5, buildRequest (harvest/lib/extract.ts:289) sends the forced tool_choice {type:'tool'}, which returns 400 on Sonnet 5.5. That would also need changing. tests/extractRequest.test.ts asserts the forced tool_choice and would need updating too.

change.title: npm @anthropic-ai/sdk 1.0.0 sends API version 2026-10-21 by default; MessageParam becomes a union, temperature/top_p/top_k removed, Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry SDKs must move to v1 too

source.quote: * **api:** add support for new API version 2026-10-21

tasks.reasoning:
package-lock.json pins @anthropic-ai/sdk at 0.125.0, which is below 1.0.0. Bumping to 1.0.0 is a single coherent move with several consequences. It changes the default anthropic-version to 2026-10-21, so any sampling params (temperature, top_p, top_k) now return 400. Document/citation placement rules change. MessageParam typing changes. OpenTelemetry auto-instrumentation turns on (introduced in 0.134.0). The scan did not read which request params extract.ts passes, so the migration agent should check for temperature/top_p/top_k and remove them, fix any MessageParam type errors, and decide on openTelemetry:false. Nothing breaks until the repo upgrades, and no retirement date for 2023-06-01 is given, so urgency is moderate and there is no hard deadline.
This task also resolves these changes. Handle each in the same change, and say in the PR how:
- anthropic:2026-10-21-api-version-2026-10-21 (api-version): New Claude API version 2026-10-21 (anthropic-version header); SDKs older than the new majors keep sending 2023-06-01. SDK 1.0.0 is the move that switches the anthropic-version header from 2023-06-01 to 2026-10-21. On 0.125.0 the repo keeps sending 2023-06-01, so the API version change only takes effect through this upgrade.
  Source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/migration-2026-10-21.md
  "This guide lists the code changes for moving from API version `2023-06-01` to `2026-10-21`."
- anthropic:2026-10-21-sampling-params-removed (field-removed): In API version 2026-10-21, temperature, top_p and top_k in Messages and Batch requests return 400. temperature, top_p and top_k return 400 only under API version 2026-10-21, which the repo adopts by upgrading to SDK 1.0.0. They are also removed from the SDK types. The same PR must strip them from the messages.create call.
  Source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/migration-2026-10-21.md
  "In `2026-10-21`, a request that sends `temperature`, `top_p`, or `top_k` returns a 400 error, even at the parameter’s default value."
- anthropic:2026-10-21-document-citations-user-assistant-errors (other): In API version 2026-10-21, document blocks in assistant messages and citations on text blocks in user messages return 400. These errors apply only under API version 2026-10-21, reached via the SDK 1.0.0 upgrade. As part of that upgrade, check whether extract.ts puts document blocks in assistant turns or citations on text blocks in user turns.
  Source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/migration-2026-10-21.md
  "In `2026-10-21`, a request that places a `document` block directly in an `assistant` message returns a 400 error."
- anthropic:2026-10-14-ts-sdk-otel-default (other): TypeScript SDK 0.134.0 auto-creates OpenTelemetry spans and trace headers if a global tracer provider exists (unsure if affects; opt out with openTelemetry:false). Automatic OpenTelemetry spans begin at 0.134.0, a version the 0.125.0→1.0.0 upgrade passes through. The upgrade PR should check for a global tracer provider and pass openTelemetry:false if spans are unwanted.
  Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-typescript/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md
  "If your app registers a global tracer provider, the SDK will create spans with it after upgrading, and they'll be exported with the rest of your traces."

callSites.why: This messages.create call is typed against MessageParam, which becomes a union in 1.0.0. It may pass temperature/top_p/top_k, which are removed from the types and rejected with 400 under the 2026-10-21 API version that 1.0.0 sends by default.

review.summary: The only named call site, harvest/lib/extract.ts:334 via buildRequest, already sends no temperature, top_p or top_k, so it needed no code change. The PR bumps @anthropic-ai/sdk to ^1.0.0 and adds a test that asserts the new anthropic-version header and the absence of sampling params. Typecheck passing against the 1.0.0 types shows the MessagesClient interface still compiles: MessageCreateParamsNonStreaming, the user message literal under the new MessageParam union, output_config, and stop_reason/stop_details. One gap remains: nothing proves the live 2026-10-21 response shape matches what extractChurch parses, because the test returns a hand-built response body. The 'verified' grade is defensible for an SDK bump with no request changes, with that caveat.

concerns.issue: The fake fetch returns a hand-written Message body. Nothing checks that a real 2026-10-21 response still has what extractChurch reads: content tool_use blocks with `input`, usage.input_tokens/output_tokens, and stop_reason values including 'refusal' with stop_details.category. Typecheck covers the declared types, not the wire format.

I could not confirm that 'claude-sonnet-5', `output_config: { effort: 'low' }` and `stop_details.category` are accepted under API version 2026-10-21. Check them against the 1.0.0 SDK types (MessageCreateParams, Message) and the API version notes in the source changelog. Typecheck passing suggests the SDK types include them.

The SDK license changes from MIT to Apache-2.0, and the SDK now pulls in @opentelemetry/api. The SDK is a devDependency, so the impact is small, but a human should acknowledge the license change. The lockfile also drops unrelated `"peer": true` flags on five packages; this looks like churn from a newer npm.
These scripts may use the SDK, directly or through createExtractor. They weren't named or shown. Typecheck would catch type breaks there, but not runtime differences in direct SDK calls.
